name: Milford Sound
bio: The legendary fiord where Mitre Peak rises from black water and waterfalls pour off sheer granite walls.

name: Doubtful Sound
bio: A vast, remote fiord reached by boat and bus over Wilmot Pass — deeper, quieter and wilder than Milford.

name: Mirror Lakes
bio: Small still tarns on the Milford Road that perfectly reflect the Earl Mountains on calm mornings.

name: Homer Tunnel
bio: A rough-hewn, 1.2 km tunnel bored through the mountains on the road to Milford, beneath towering cirque walls.

name: Te Anau Glowworm Caves
bio: A boat across Lake Te Anau leads to young limestone caves where a silent punt drifts beneath glowworm grottos.

name: Milford Track
bio: The 'finest walk in the world', a four-day Great Walk over Mackinnon Pass past Sutherland Falls to Milford Sound.

name: Kepler Track
bio: A Great Walk loop from Te Anau along an exposed alpine ridge high above the lakes, walkable in day sections.

name: Routeburn Track
bio: An alpine Great Walk between Fiordland and Mount Aspiring; from The Divide, Key Summit makes a superb day hike.

name: Te Anau
bio: The lakeside town that is the main base for Fiordland, Milford Sound and the Kepler Track.

name: The Chasm
bio: A 20-minute return walk off the Milford Road to the Cleddau River pouring through rock sculpted into basins.

name: Key Summit
bio: A climb from The Divide on the Routeburn Track to an alpine wetland with views of the Darran Mountains.

name: Lake Marian
bio: A 3.1 km track from Hollyford Road past waterfalls to an alpine lake in a hanging valley, about 1 hr 30 min each way.

name: Manapōuri
bio: A lakeside township 20 minutes from Te Anau, where boats cross Lake Manapouri for Doubtful Sound.

name: Bowen Falls
bio: At 162 m the tallest permanent waterfall into Milford Sound, reached from the wharf by a short boat hop and a walk.

name: Hollyford Track
bio: A 56 km, 4 to 5 day tramp down the Hollyford Valley to Martins Bay, with no alpine sections to close it in snow.

name: Monkey Creek
bio: A roadside stop on the Milford Road at a mountain stream, known for chances to spot kea and blue duck.

name: Lake Gunn
bio: A beech-forest lake in the Eglinton Valley with an easy 45-minute loop walk from Cascade Creek.

name: Sutherland Falls
bio: One of New Zealand's tallest waterfalls, 580 m in three cascades, a 90-minute side walk off the Milford Track.

name: Ulva Island
bio: A predator-free open sanctuary where saddleback, rifleman and Stewart Island robins flit around your feet.

name: Rakiura Track
bio: A three-day Great Walk loop through rimu forest and along golden beaches from Oban.

name: Observation Rock
bio: A short climb above Oban to a granite outcrop with sunset views over Paterson Inlet.

name: Mason Bay
bio: A remote 20 km beach of dunes on the wild west coast, where Stewart Island kiwi forage even by day.

name: E Hayes and Sons
bio: A working hardware store displaying Burt Munro's record-breaking Indian motorcycle among hundreds of classic machines.

name: Bill Richardson Transport World
bio: One of the largest private collections of trucks and vehicles in the world, with a quirky WOW wearable-art gallery.

name: Queens Park
bio: An 80-hectare park of rose gardens, an aviary and an animal enclosure at the heart of the city.

name: Stirling Point
bio: Bluff's famous signpost at the end of State Highway 1, pointing to cities around the world.

name: Hump Ridge Track
bio: A 60 km walk, opened as a Great Walk in 2024, climbing the Hump Ridge from Rarakau on the south coast.

name: Clifden Suspension Bridge
bio: An 1899 suspension bridge, 111.5 m long, over the Waiau River, with its original wooden deck, now for walkers.
